create.name: Martine Batchelor
create.bio:
Martine Batchelor is a French-born meditation teacher and writer who spent ten years as a Buddhist nun in South Korea, training in Seon (Korean Zen) under Master Kusan at Songgwangsa and later translating his book The Way of Korean Zen. After his death she gave back her vows and returned to Europe, where she also took up mindfulness practice in the Insight tradition. She now lives with her husband Stephen Batchelor in a village outside Bordeaux, teaches on the faculty of Bodhi College and is a long-standing teacher and patron at Gaia House in Devon.

Her teaching is plain, exact and practical. She often works with the Seon practice of asking 'What is this?', with mindfulness of feeling tones (vedanā), and with the four heart qualities of friendliness, compassion, joy and equanimity, always asking how they help in everyday life. Her books include Meditation for Life, Let Go, a guide to working with habit patterns, The Spirit of the Buddha, Women in Korean Zen, and What Is This?, written with Stephen. She leads retreats and short courses, mostly in Europe, in person and online, and like many in her tradition she offers her teaching on a donation basis.

books.title: Meditation for Life
books.author: Martine Batchelor
books.description: A clear introduction to Buddhist meditation covering posture, breath, concentration, enquiry and loving-kindness, with guidance on bringing practice into ordinary days. The first edition carried photographs by Stephen Batchelor.

books.title: Let Go: A Buddhist Guide to Breaking Free of Habits
books.author: Martine Batchelor
books.description: She looks at how habits of mind and behaviour form and repeat, and offers meditative ways to meet them with curiosity rather than force. Each chapter closes with a short practice.

books.title: The Spirit of the Buddha
books.author: Martine Batchelor
books.description: A short primer on the Buddha's core teachings for general readers, from Yale University Press. It sets out the main ideas and shows how they can be lived today.

books.title: What Is This?: Ancient Questions for Modern Minds
books.author: Martine Batchelor, Stephen Batchelor
books.description: Drawn from talks the two authors gave on a Seon retreat in England, the book explains the Korean Zen practice of asking 'What is this?' and how open questioning can become a way of life.

books.title: Women in Korean Zen: Lives and Practices
books.author: Martine Batchelor
books.description: Part memoir of her own decade as a nun in Korea and part life story of the senior nun Son'gyong Sunim, this book gives a rare view of women's monastic practice in Korean Seon.

courses.title: Feeling and Flourishing
courses.description: A two-evening online course from Gaia House on mindfulness of feeling tones. The first session looks at how experience is felt as pleasant, unpleasant or neutral; the second links this to the four heart qualities as a way to react less and see more clearly.
courses.price: £44 GBP (standard rate; £30, £15 and free places also offered)

free_resources.title: What is this? (free taster)
free_resources.description: A free sample of the book she wrote with Stephen Batchelor, introducing the Seon practice of asking 'What is this?'.

free_resources.title: The Little Lazy Guide to Awakening
free_resources.description: A page of short, playful verses she wrote as reminders for practice, about openness, simplicity and not grasping. They are meant to be read slowly, one at a time.

free_resources.title: Reading Group Guide for What is this?
free_resources.description: A free PDF of discussion questions for groups reading What Is This? together, chapter by chapter.
